The West Midland Combined Authority seeks the services of a skilled consultant(s) from the Transport Sector, to deliver support with the development of the statutory West Midlands Local Transport Plan (WMLTP5).
The need for this work is to help WMCA translate the strategic intent of Journeys for Everyone, the West Midlands Growth Plan, the Integrated Settlement Outcomes Framework and the emerging Rosewell Review programme approach into a coherent investment proposition that can support consultation, assurance, funding decisions and future delivery.

lots.description:
The appointed consultant must-
I.	Translate the outputs of the Rosewell Review into four (4) ABIP's into the into the WMLTP5 for Coventry, the Black Country, Birmingham and Solihull.
II.	Set out the delivery programme of investment priorities consisting of a mix of Capital (CDEL) and Revenue (RDEL) measures to support WM Growth Plan and WMLTP5 aims to improve accessibility, reduce overall levels of traffic and reduce transports impacts on the environment in line with the ISOF.
III.	Define a prioritised transport delivery programme for 2027/28 onwards.
IV.	Deliver the prioritisation of the programme, which will be largely fixed, however, will require using a range of tools the programme should be modelled to provide an assessment of:
a)	Impacts on travel demand
b)	Impacts on mode share
c)	Connectivity / accessibility (and relevant wider social and distributional impacts).
d)	Wider Economic Benefits 
e)	Wider Health Benefits
f)	Wider Environmental Benefits
g)	Carbon Impacts

tender.title: Employability Services Procured Service Arrangement - Phase 2
tender.description:
The Council is seeking to appoint service providers through a Procured Service Arrangement (PSA).  This is a bespoke arrangement/flexible framework which will be developed primarily for Employability Services but can be accessed by all services within the Council.
The PSA will be procured using the “light touch” procedure set out in Regulations 74 -76 of the Public Contracts (Scotland) Regulations 2015 (“the 2015 Regulations”). This allows the Council to carry out a selection process which adopts the principles of equal treatment, non-discrimination and transparency and complies with procurement best practice without requiring the use of the traditional open or restricted procedure set out in the 2015 Regulations.
The PSA has a broad scope of service delivery with the opportunity for many providers to be appointed. There is no limit on the number of providers who can be appointed to any of the lots under the PSA. The PSA remains open for its lifetime which  allows for new providers to be added over its  term, at regular intervals which will be advised by the Council.  Applicants to the PSA will be evaluated in ‘Phases’, based on the closing date for each Phase.  Following the closing of each Phase, the PSA will re-open for new applications for the next Phase.

lots.description: The University of Edinburgh is seeking to award Oxford Instruments the contract for the purchase of a 2D Materials Processing Suite to establish a new research capability within the University's cleanroom, enabling the growth and processing of atomically thin materials, including graphene, molybdenum disulphide (MoS₂), tungsten disulphide (WS₂) and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). The suite requires two complementary systems: a plasma-assisted Chemical Vapour Deposition (CVD) system for growing these materials, and an Ion Beam Etching (IBE) system for precisely removing selected areas of material to produce functional devices.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The University requires a 2D Materials Processing Suite to establish a new cleanroom capability for growing and processing atomically thin materials, including graphene, molybdenum disulphide (MoS₂), tungsten disulphide (WS₂) and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN).
The suite must comprise two complementary systems:
- Plasma-assisted Chemical Vapour Deposition (CVD) system: Must incorporate a loadlock, support a minimum eight-line gas delivery system, enable the growth of graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides, and operate at temperatures up to 1,200°C.
- Ion Beam Etching (IBE) system: Must provide sub-nanometre etching precision, Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) endpoint detection and Chemical Assisted Ion Beam Etching (CAIBE) using fluorine-based chemistry.
- A critical requirement is a retractable SIMS probe that can be safely withdrawn during CAIBE processing to prevent damage from highly reactive gases, while retaining endpoint detection capability during conventional etching processes.
Oxford Instruments has been identified as the only manufacturer able to provide a combined solution meeting all the specified technical requirements, particularly the integration of SIMS endpoint detection with a retractable probe capable of supporting CAIBE processing.
This functionality is essential for accurately processing extremely thin materials, where conventional plasma etching risks removing underlying material. The proposed equipment will establish the required 2D materials research capability while also enhancing existing thin-film processing workflows within the University's cleanroom.

tender.description:

This contract focuses on the delivery of community dermatology services, helping to manage patient demand closer to home and reducing pressures on secondary care providers where clinically appropriate. The service forms part of the wider dermatology pathway and works collaboratively with acute providers to ensure patients requiring specialist or hospital-based interventions are referred appropriately. 
The commissioning responsibility for this contract transferred to Essex ICB as part of the ICB reorganisation in April 2026.

Quality & Innovation 40%.

It is essential for good collaboration between provider, primary and secondary care

Access to community services are important to ensure not all patients are referred into an acute setting where appropriate
Social Value 5%.
Although the main focus of the specialist fertility service is to provide healthcare, a weighting of 5% has been allocated to reflect the ICB priority towards the importance of social value
Key criteria were specified, and assessment against each criterion was assessed based as above and on the current service delivery model and performance. and the supplier meets all the requirements specified to the satisfaction of the ICB, and it is expected that they will satisfy the requirements of the new contract.

tender.title: Penetration Testing
tender.description:
The Planning Inspectorate is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced suppliers for the provision of penetration testing services. As a Public Sector organisation, we recognise the importance of safeguarding our information assets, protecting our infrastructure, and ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of our systems and data. 
In response to the evolving cyber threat landscape and the need to maintain robust security assurance, the Planning Inspectorate's requires the delivery of penetration testing services to proactively identify vulnerabilities, assess the effectiveness of existing security controls, improve resilience across services, and mitigate risks posed by potential cyber threats. 
Through the identification and remediation of vulnerabilities, the services will assist in reducing the likelihood of a costly data breach or disruption to business operations, and in turn enable the appropriate identification, assessment, and management of cyber risk across the organisation. 
This requirement is also informed by applicable security and regulatory expectations, including alignment with recognised government guidance and assurance schemes for penetration testing, ensuring that Planning Inspectorate continues to meet expected standards for secure system operation and risk management.

lots.description:
Web Application, Application Programming Interface (API), Infrastructure, Large Language Model (LLM), and Cloud Testing (including Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure environments) 
The supplier shall conduct thorough and methodical penetration testing across Web Applications, Application Programming Interfaces, internal and external infrastructure, Large Language Model implementations, and cloud platforms (including Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure). This shall include both authenticated and unauthenticated testing, as well as internal and external perspectives, to ensure a comprehensive assessment of the organisation's attack surface. 
Internal and external testing coverage 
Testing shall encompass both external threat scenarios (simulating attacks from outside the organisation) and internal threat scenarios (simulating insider threats or compromised credentials), ensuring a holistic evaluation of security posture across all layers of the environment. 
Vulnerability validation and re-testing 
The supplier shall validate identified vulnerabilities through controlled exploitation techniques to confirm their existence and potential impact. Following remediation, the supplier shall perform re-testing activities to verify that vulnerabilities have been effectively addressed and that no residual risk remains. 
Authorisation and non-disruptive testing 
All testing activities must be formally authorised in advance and conducted in a controlled and non-disruptive manner, ensuring no adverse impact on live services, business operations, or data integrity. The supplier shall adhere to agreed rules of engagement, change control processes, and escalation procedures throughout the engagement. Additional information: This is a Call-off contract from GCA Framework RM3764.3 Cyber Security Services 3, Dynamic Purchasing System under PCR 2015.

The award decision-makers for this process were representatives of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board.
The contract is for the provision of optometry services at HMP Cardiff. The decision to utilise the Most Suitable Provider Process and select the incumbent provider was based on the following considerations:
- The provider currently delivers the optometry service at HMP Cardiff and is fully operational within the prison setting.
- Continuity and stability of service provision are important to ensure uninterrupted access to healthcare within HMP Cardiff.
- The provider has established safeguarding, governance, reporting and operational arrangements which are embedded within the service and enable service delivery to continue safely and efficiently.
- Appointment of the incumbent provider avoids service disruption, mobilisation risks and delays associated with transitioning to a new provider.
- The review of contract performance found that the provider has consistently delivered all commissioned clinics, maintained a positive safety record and developed effective operational relationships within HMP Cardiff.
In determining the most suitable provider, the decision-makers placed particular importance on service continuity, operational readiness, patient safety, governance arrangements, service quality and the ability to continue delivering care without disruption. These considerations were judged to be of greater significance than the potential benefits of undertaking a provider transition given the specialist prison environment and the risks associated with service interruption.
The review identified opportunities for improvement which will be addressed through a renewed agreement, including strengthened KPIs, enhanced monitoring of waiting times and service utilisation, management of DNA rates, revised reporting requirements and consideration of service redesign to improve access and value for money.
No providers were excluded from the process.
The contract has not been awarded to an excluded provider.

tender.description: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board is seeking a provider to deliver comprehensive optometry services at HMP Cardiff, including eye examinations, diagnosis and management of visual and ocular conditions, provision of spectacles where required, and referrals to secondary care. The service will support equitable access to high-quality eye care for prisoners and contribute to improved health and well-being outcomes within the custodial setting.

lots.description:
Cardiff and Vale University Health Board intends to award a contract under the Most Suitable Provider Process for the provision of comprehensive optometry services at HMP Cardiff.
This is an existing service with an existing provider that will continue to provide timely access to routine and clinically necessary eye care for the prison population. The intention is to award the contract to an existing provider, subject to completion of the Provider Selection Regime (PSR) requirements and approval processes.
The contract is intended to commence on 01/12/2026 and continue for an initial period of one year, with the option, at the Health Board's discretion, to extend for up to two further periods of 12 months.
The service will provide routine sight tests, assessment, diagnosis and management of visual and ocular conditions, provision of spectacles where clinically required, and referral to secondary care ophthalmology services where appropriate. The provider will deliver regular on-site clinics within HMP Cardiff and will supply all necessary equipment, consumables and professional expertise required to undertake examinations and deliver patient-centred optometry care.
The provider will be expected to work collaboratively with prison healthcare teams to support effective care pathways, continuity of care, accurate clinical record keeping and timely referral management. The service aims to improve visual health outcomes for prisoners, many of whom present with unmet eye care needs upon entry into custody. By supporting the early identification, treatment and ongoing management of eye conditions, the service contributes to improved health, wellbeing, participation in education and rehabilitation activities, and overall quality of life within the prison environment.
Services will be delivered in accordance with all relevant professional, clinical and regulatory requirements, including applicable standards of the General Optical Council and NHS Wales policies. The contract will be subject to appropriate contract management and performance monitoring arrangements to ensure the delivery of safe, effective and high-quality services throughout the contract term.

tender.procurementMethodRationale:
The contract was awarded without prior publication of a contract notice on the basis that competition is absent for technical reasons.
The contract consolidates and co-terminates three existing software services that are already supplied by the contractor and are embedded within the University's operational and business processes. The services form part of the University's existing software environment and are integrated with established configurations, user permissions, workflows, reporting arrangements and support arrangements.
Awarding the contract to an alternative supplier would require migration from the incumbent systems, significant reconfiguration, data migration activities, user retraining, implementation of replacement solutions and disruption to established operational processes. The University concluded that changing supplier would create substantial technical difficulties and material risks to the continuity, stability and effectiveness of these critical services.
The University considered the available options and determined that only the incumbent supplier could provide the required continuation of the existing services without disproportionate technical disruption. The direct award therefore ensures continuity of service and maintains the integrity of the University's existing software environment.
As part of the award, the University has aligned the contract terms for the three services into a single co-termed arrangement, which simplifies contract management and delivers improved commercial value. However, the principal justification for the absence of competition for technical reasons and the need to maintain continuity of the University's established software services.

tender.description:
NHS Essex Integrated Care Board (herein "the Authority")'s intention to award contracts to deliver Specialist Fertility Services to the patients within NHS Essex's  ICB geographical footprint. The contract will be for 12 months months from 01st April 2027 - 31st March 2028.  The aggregate contract values are below inclusive VAT noting that these are zero value contracts – paid at local prices- based on planning values for 2026-27 and will be subject to any agreed growth and inflator/deflators applicable to 2027/28.

Quality & Innovation 40%. 
Quality should be the primary consideration for specialist fertility services due to the highly regulated nature of assisted conception treatment, the clinical risks associated with fertility interventions and the importance of achieving safe, effective patient outcomes. Innovation remains important, particularly in supporting improvements in patient experience, clinical outcomes, efficiency and access to treatment. However, any innovation must operate within established regulatory and clinical frameworks and should not compromise the quality, safety or effectiveness of care.
Value 30%.
It is a statutory duty to ensure the best use of public resources, therefore value has the second highest weighting
Integration, Collaboration & Service Sustainability 15%,
It is essential for good collaboration between specialist fertility services and secondary care
Access Health Inequalities and Choice 10%;
Access to specialist services are important to ensure all patients receive the appropriate care and treatment
Social Value 5%.
Although the main focus of the specialist fertility service is to provide healthcare, a weighting of 5% has been allocated to reflect the ICB priority towards the importance of social value

The Authority intends to award this contract via Direct Award Process C under the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and Procurement Act 2023 do not apply. NHS Essex Integrated Care Board is the Relevant Authority undertaking this process. The services comprise the provision of  Specialist Fertility Services. Infertility is defined as a failure to conceive after regular unprotected
sexual intercourse in the absence of known reproductive pathology.
The management of infertility falls into 3 main types:
1. Medical treatment to restore fertility (for example, the use of drugs for
ovulation induction)
2. Surgical treatment to restore fertility (for example, laparoscopy for
ablation of endometriosis)
3. Assisted reproduction techniques – any treatment that deals with
means of conception other than vaginal coitus. It frequently involves
the handling of gametes or embryos and mainly includes in vitro
fertilisation (IVF), intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI), and Donor
Insemination (DI). The specialist fertility services to be provided to patients fulfilling the eligibility
criteria include:
1. In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) with or without Intra-cytoplasmic Sperm
Injection (ICSI)
2. Frozen Embryo Transfer
3. Embryo/Blastocyst Freezing and Storage (Gametes)
4. Surgical sperm recovery (Testicular Epididymal Sperm Aspiration
(TESA) / Percutaneous Sperm Aspiration (PESA) including storage
where required)
5. Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) unstimulated
6. Donor Oocyte Cycle
7. Donor Sperm Insemination, with IVF/IUI. Donor insemination in
following conditions: obstructive azoospermia, non-obstructive
azoospermia, severe deficits in semen quality in couples who do not wish to undergo ICSI, where there is a high risk of transmitting
infectious disease to the offspring or woman from the man
8. Oocyte retrieval for patients undergoing cancer treatments –
includes first years’ storage
9. Oocyte or sperm annual storage for patients undergoing cancer
treatment1.
10. Egg donation where no other treatment
is available: The patient
must be able to provide a donor; alternatively, the patient can be
placed on the waiting list until a donor becomes available. This
waiting list will be monitored separately to the general IVF waiting
list.
11. Specialist courier transportation of stored gametes between NHS
providers where an eligible patient chooses to transfer their NHS
treatment. This will also apply to patients choosing to transfer from
a private clinic to NHS clinic in order to comply with the MSE ICB
policy.
The above services shall be provided in line with HFEA regulations
The providers are existing providers of these services to NHS Essex Integrated Care Board and has demonstrated their ability to deliver the services to the required standard, following assessment against the five key Provider Selection Regime criteria.

tender.description: Health Roster, Medical Roster & Job Planning Software & Support

lots.description:
The procurement is for the implementation of a single Trust-wide medical e-rostering solution to replace the Trust's current fragmented and predominantly manual medical rostering arrangements. Existing processes do not meet operational requirements or NHS England standards, resulting in rota inaccuracies, clinic cancellations, increased temporary staffing costs, and significant administrative effort.
The proposed solution will provide a unified platform for managing medical workforce rostering across the Trust, delivering functionality including automated payroll reconciliation, roster generation, safe-working compliance monitoring, sickness management, contracted hours recording, and integration with job planning and temporary staffing systems. The system will improve workforce visibility, strengthen governance, support safe staffing, and ensure compliance with national e-rostering standards.
For consultants and resident doctors, the solution will enhance roster accuracy, improve leave management, support flexible working arrangements, facilitate publication of rotas at least six weeks in advance, and reduce scheduling conflicts through integration with job planning processes.
Following the expiry of the Trust's Agenda for Change e-Rostering contract on 31 August 2026, the Trust identified an opportunity to implement a single workforce rostering platform encompassing both Agenda for Change and Medical staff groups. This approach delivers a modest cost saving compared with current combined rostering expenditure while maximising operational efficiencies, enhancing system integration, and improving workforce management through the adoption of a unified rostering solution across the entire Trust workforce.

This is a Provider Selection Regime (PSR) intention to award notice. The awarding of this contract is subject to the Health Care Services (Provider Selection Regime) Regulations 2023. For the avoidance of doubt, the provisions of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 do not apply to this award. The standstill period begins on the day after the publication of this notice. Representations by providers must be made to the relevant authority by 13th November 2026. This contract has not yet formally been awarded; this notice serves as an intention to award a contract under the competitive process of the PSR.
Written representations should be sent to Procurement@brighton-hove.gov.uk
Award decision-makers: Director of Public Health and Corporate Director - Families, Children and Wellbeing
Conflict of interests: No conflict of interests or potential conflict of interests were identified throughout the procurement process.
Relative importance of key criteria:
The below statement explains the relative importance of the key criteria that was used to make the decision, alongside the rationale for the relative importance of the key criteria. The provider that the Council intends to award the contract to is the highest scoring bidder against the published key criteria. 
Criterion 1 is awarded the greatest weighting (35%) to ensure that the service delivers high-quality, safe, effective, evidence-based treatment and recovery support that improves outcomes for individuals affected by substance use. The service must provide a comprehensive range of interventions, including harm reduction, treatment, recovery support, and safeguarding, whilst maintaining a strong focus on service user experience, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Brighton & Hove experiences significant levels of substance-related harm, including drug and alcohol dependency, drug-related deaths, alcohol-related hospital admissions, and associated health and social inequalities. Substance use disproportionately affects people experiencing deprivation, homelessness, mental ill-health, involvement with the criminal justice system, and other forms of disadvantage. To address these challenges, Criterion 4 quality and innovation has been awarded the weighting of (15%).
The successful delivery of substance use treatment and recovery services relies upon effective partnership working across a complex system of health, social care, housing, criminal justice, and voluntary and community sector organisations. Integrated working is essential to improve outcomes, support recovery, reduce harm, and ensure continuity of care. Criterion 3, integration, collaboration and service sustainability, is therefore assigned a weighting of 20%.
Criterion 2, value, is assigned a weighting of 20% on the basis that the service model specified represents good value for money and supports the efficient use of public resources through the delivery of evidence-based interventions that reduce wider system costs associated with healthcare utilisation, homelessness, safeguarding, and criminal justice involvement.
A weighting of 10% is assigned to Criterion 5, social value, to ensure due regard is given to opportunities to improve economic, social, and environmental wellbeing through the delivery of the contract, including supporting local employment, workforce development, community resilience, and environmental sustainability.
Criterion 1: Quality and Innovation
Weight: 35%
Rationale for weighting
A service that consistently delivers safe, effective, person-centred, and evidence-based substance use treatment and recovery support is essential. The service must operate in accordance with national guidance, clinical standards, and best practice, achieving positive outcomes for individuals, families, and communities.
The service must provide a comprehensive range of interventions, including assessment, harm reduction, psychosocial interventions, prescribing and recovery support, whilst ensuring strong safeguarding arrangements and effective risk management. The service should be accessible, responsive to service user needs, and positively regarded by people accessing support.
The provider will demonstrate innovation in the delivery of treatment and recovery services, using evidence-based approaches to improve engagement, retention, recovery outcomes, and the prevention of drug- and alcohol-related harm.
Criterion 2: Value
Weight: 20%
Rationale for weighting
Delivery of the specified service represents cost-effective use of public resources. Effective substance use treatment and recovery services reduce demand on healthcare, social care, housing, criminal justice, and other public services by preventing escalation of need and supporting sustained recovery.
The service requires appropriately qualified and experienced clinical and non-clinical staff to deliver safe and effective interventions. Workforce costs constitute a significant proportion of overall expenditure and are largely determined by nationally recognised pay frameworks and professional requirements. This reduces the risk of poor value for money whilst ensuring that service quality and safety are maintained.
The provider must demonstrate efficient use of resources and the ability to maximise outcomes within the available budget.
Criterion 3: Integration, Collaboration and Service Sustainability
Weight: 20%
Rationale for weighting
National policy and evidence highlight the importance of integrated, whole-system approaches to substance use treatment and recovery.
The service must work in close collaboration with a wide range of partners, including primary care, acute and mental health services, housing providers, criminal justice agencies, social care, safeguarding services, employment and skills providers, and voluntary and community sector organisations.
Effective integration is essential to ensure coordinated pathways of care, support individuals with multiple and complex needs, and improve outcomes across the wider system. The service must also contribute to the long-term sustainability of the local treatment and recovery system through workforce development, partnership working, and continuous service improvement.
Criterion 4: Improving Access, Reducing Health Inequalities and Facilitating Choice
Weight: 15%
Rationale for weighting
Substance-related harm is not distributed equally across the population and is strongly associated with deprivation, social exclusion, trauma, poor mental health, homelessness, and other forms of disadvantage.
The service must provide equitable and timely access to treatment and recovery support for all residents who need it, including those who experience the greatest barriers to accessing services. Particular attention should be given to underserved groups, including people experiencing homelessness, individuals involved in the criminal justice system, people with co-occurring mental health needs, minority ethnic communities, women, young adults transitioning into adult services, and people with protected characteristics.
The service should offer flexible and accessible models of delivery, enabling individuals to access support in ways that best meet their needs and preferences. The provider must actively work to reduce inequalities in access, engagement, and outcomes, and develop strong partnerships with community organisations to improve reach and support underserved populations.
Criterion 5: Social Value
Weight: 10%
Rationale for weighting
The provider should contribute positively to the economic, social, and environmental wellbeing of Brighton & Hove through the delivery of the contract.
This includes supporting local employment and skills development, creating opportunities for people with lived experience to participate in service delivery and workforce development, strengthening community capacity, and promoting volunteering and peer support.
The delivery of high-quality employment opportunities, workforce wellbeing initiatives, and community-based recovery support networks will contribute significant social value alongside the core objectives of the service.

tender.title: Substance Use Service - Core Drug and alcohol service and inpatient detoxification
tender.description:
Brighton & Hove City Council (BHCC) is commissioning an integrated drug and alcohol treatment system aligned to national policy, including the UK Drug Strategy (2021), Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) guidance, Public Health Outcomes Framework (PHOF), and National Drug Treatment Monitoring System (NDTMS) requirements.
This notice is an intention to award a contract under the competitive process.

lots.description:
This notice is an intention to award a contract under the competitive process. 
The required services will be fully integrated, this means the provider will deliver services that a range of clinical, psychosocial, inpatient and recovery support interventions. This includes the management of accessing and the pathway into inpatient detoxification. The primary function of the inpatient provision will be to offer flexible short stay for substance dependent service users, providing medically supervised prescribing, intensive assessment, care and treatment with brief intervention therapy to those service users who require stabilisation, reduction or detoxification from harmful substances.
In BHCC we want everyone to have the best possible life, we want everyone to be included, and no-one should be left behind. This will be achieved by ensuring commissioned services are recovery focussed, work at the centre of communities and can engage with all residents who need support. This specification sets out the requirements for services in line with a recovery focused drug, alcohol and inpatient treatment system and details the objectives and interventions to address drug and alcohol related needs.
BHCC wishes to build on the current adult drug and alcohol service which will enable a whole system and preventative approach, subsequently increasing the number of people aspiring to recovery from dependence. This will be achieved by providing individual support and treatment packages of care reducing the harm caused by addiction and dependence, to enable this to happen the provider will work in a treatment system that includes primary care, secondary, tertiary and criminal justice agencies working together to reduce harms and increase recovery.
The contract is for 5 years with optional extension options of an additional 2 years (Total contract term of 7 years)
The total estimated contract value indicated in this notice is for the full 7 year contract term.
This contract is being funded via a Public Health grant.

tender.title: Independent review into 2DP fire/structural safety
tender.description:
The Education Estates Directorate (EED) within the Department for Education (DfE) continually review the standards and assurance processes used to deliver school and college buildings through our capital delivery programmes.
2D panelised construction is a type of Modern Methods of Construction (MMC). MMC is a broad term used for innovative technologies and practices to improve speed, efficiency and sustainability in construction. In 2019, MHCLG developed a definition framework for MMC. In summary:
• Category 1 – Volumetric Modular – 3D Primary Structural Systems
• Category 2 – Panelised Modular – 2D Primary Structural Systems
• Category 3 to 7 – Other manufacturing process (including 3D printing, digital systems and non-structural components).
This contract will support a wider review to see where improvements can be made to the department’s current approach to delivering buildings using load-bearing 2D panelised construction. This will ensure we continue to deliver buildings that provide an excellent learning environment.

lots.description: The successful Supplier, as set out in this notice, shall provide the department with strategic technical advice on fire safety and structural engineering considerations for the delivery of buildings using 2D panelised construction. The advice shall be based on findings and evidence from a review of existing education projects constructed using 2D panels. Suppliers shall undertake a desk review, site visits and stakeholder workshops (with manufacturers, suppliers, delivery colleagues). The Supplier shall also draw on their wider experience and expertise of this construction type across other sectors (including residential, commercial, healthcare and the wider public sector) when providing this technical advice.
